t_origin: t = frame_index / fps, frame 0 = first frame of the clip
convention: meters; origin = center dot; +x along the long axis toward the net at the top of the screen; +y = screen left (x then y counterclockwise on screen); z not observable (always 0)
scale_source: ICE-PLANE scale for puck motion: params.json rink_length = 60 m (PLACEHOLDER, unmeasured) / inner board length 913.00 px x (1 + k_board +0.00000); the board outline is at ice level within k_board = -0.00244 +- 0.00144, so board and ice scales agree. Puck positions are blob centroids reprojected to the ground (see track.json puck_parallax).
what: player body = pink disc; position = centre of an ellipse fitted to the convex hull of the pink blob, minus the frame's camera shift (reference ice pixels)
camera_follows_player: the game camera follows the player: the disc stays at the image centre and the player's motion is the camera's motion, measured on the faceoff-dot landmarks
confidence: exp(-0.5 (ln(area/area_ref)/0.25)^2) * roundness score * fill score; 0 for interpolated rows

height_correction.area_model: not fittable: the disc never leaves the image centre (r range 1.7 px)
height_correction.reason: no height correction: the disc stays within 0.9 px (p99) of the image centre (the camera follows the player), so k/2*r < 0.046 px even with k = 10x the puck's, below the centroid noise; and where r varies the blob does not grow with r
